extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners and applicants on entry, disapproval, and treatment of preliminary amendments, supplemental replies, fully-responsive replies, amendments after final, fee/payment and form requirements, and related procedural matters during patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment entry/disapproval baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment filed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 will be entered unless it is disapproved by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment will be disapproved if it cancels all the claims in the application without presenting any new or substitute claims (Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co.; 37 CFR 1.115(b)). A preliminary amendment may also be disapproved if it unduly interferes with the preparation of an Office action. If disapproved for cancelling all claims, the Office will send a notice of non-compliant amendment and treat the application as containing only a single claim for fee calculation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits for preliminary amendments to avoid disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment will not be disapproved under 37 CFR 1.115(b)(2) if it is filed no later than specified statutory periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed filing windows: (i) three months from the filing date of an application under 37 CFR 1.53(b); (ii) the filing date of a continued prosecution application under 37 CFR 1.53(d); or (iii) three months from the date the national stage is entered under 37 CFR 1.491 in an international application. These time periods are not extendable (37 CFR 1.115(b)(3)–(4)). Applicants are encouraged to file preliminary amendments as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered when denying entry for undue interference
rubrics_metrics.description: When denying entry of a preliminary amendment for unduly interfering with preparation of an Office action, consider the state of preparation of the first Office action and the nature of any changes resulting from entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically consider (A) the state of preparation of a first Office action as of the date of receipt (37 CFR 1.6) of the preliminary amendment, and (B) the nature of any changes to the specification or claims that would result from entry of the preliminary amendment. If these show undue interference, entry may be denied (requires SPE approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-condition test for denying entry of preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry of a preliminary amendment that would unduly interfere with preparation of an Office action may be denied only if two conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition 1: the examiner has devoted a significant amount of time to preparation of an Office action before the amendment is received. Condition 2: entry of the amendment would require the examiner to spend significant additional time (e.g., another prior art search or extensive revision of the Office action). If both are met, obtain SPE approval before denying entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of amendment contents that may cause significant additional examiner time
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of amendment changes that, if inserted, would likely require significant additional examiner time and thus may support denial of entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: amends the claims; adds numerous new claims; amends the specification to change the scope of the claims; amends the specification so that a new matter issue would be raised; includes arguments; includes an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.132; includes evidence traversing rejections from a prior Office action in the parent application. This list is not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where disapproval of preliminary amendment is inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry should not be denied if the examiner has not devoted significant time or entry would not require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner has not started working on the Office action or has only inspected the file for formal requirements, the examiner should enter and consider the preliminary amendment. Even if significant time has been spent, entry should not be disapproved if the amendment merely cancels some pending claims, amends claims to overcome 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, amends claims to place application in condition for allowance, or only includes changes previously suggested by the examiner that do not require significant additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendment cancelling all claims without substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that cancels all claims without presenting any new or substitute claims will not be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an amendment will not be entered and will not deny the application a filing date solely because it was submitted. The Office will treat the application as containing a single claim for fee purposes and will send a notice of non-compliant amendment (37 CFR 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.46 for denial due to undue interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.46 to notify applicant that entry of a preliminary amendment is denied because it unduly interferes with preparation of the Office action (37 CFR 1.115(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form should state the date received, what the examiner had completed when the amendment was received, and how entry would require significant additional time. Examiner notes: use 37 CFR 1.6 receipt date; describe state of preparation (e.g., claim analysis, prior art search, drafting awaiting SPE approval); explain additional time (e.g., need to search another classification area or extensively revise the Office action). Suggest resubmission with a responsive reply to ensure proper entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for replies to be fully responsive (37 CFR 1.111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the reply must be in writing and distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors and reply to every ground of objection and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specific distinctions does not comply. The reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or reexamination to final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must point out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed to be present and show how amendments avoid cited references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies to new or rewritten claims presented in reply. Failure to point out patentable novelty may lead to the amendment being held not fully responsive and a time period set to furnish a proper reply; if claims remain clearly open to rejection, a final rejection should generally be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reply / traverse of requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where reply to a requirement is necessary for further consideration or allowable subject matter has been indicated, a complete reply must comply with formal requirements or specifically traverse each one not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal matters (drawings corrections, new oath) are generally considered formal, but the line with merits is not sharp. Examiner may insist on such corrections prior to indicating allowable subject matter if merits determination requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment options for amendments not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may accept the amendment as adequate, notify applicant to complete the reply within the remaining period, or set a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice depends on whether amendment is bona fide, whether there is sufficient time to cure within the reply period, and the nature of the deficiency. If minor omission and sufficient time remains, notify applicant (preferably by telephone) to supply omission within remaining time; if insufficient time, set a new 2-month period under 37 CFR 1.135(c). Examiner should not further examine on merits until omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: When 37 CFR 1.135(c) (new time period) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) authorizes giving a new time period only when the reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and a required matter was inadvertently omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not apply when omission was deliberate or when applicant is abusing the practice to obtain additional time. Examples of non-applicability: deliberate omission of required election of species, amendment cancelling all claims without substitutes, or other deliberate failures. Once inadvertence is called to applicant's attention, it no longer exists and a second 2-month time period under 1.135(c) is not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and options when 1.135(c) period is set
rubrics_metrics.description: If a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) is set, applicant must supply the omission within that period (or extensions under 1.136) to avoid abandonment; applicant may file a continuing application during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If insufficient time remains to cure within the original reply period, the examiner should set the 2-month period. Failure to timely supply omission leads to abandonment unless applicant files continuing application or otherwise responds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of 1.135(c) after final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving a new time period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; otherwise they are not approved for entry. Examiner may request authorization for an examiner's amendment to correct omission and place application in condition for allowance; examiner may also withdraw finality and reopen prosecution, at discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 7.95 and 7.95.01 for bona fide but non-responsive replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.95 to notify applicant when a bona fide reply is not fully responsive and give a shortened statutory TWO (2) MONTHS period to supply omissions; use 7.95.01 to indicate lack of arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.95 explains omissions and warns about abandonment; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be granted but cannot extend beyond statute maximum. 7.95.01 requires applicant to submit arguments under 'Remarks' explaining disagreements and how claims avoid applied references. Examiner notes: 7.95 should be used where a bona fide reply is not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies entry limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply that is supplemental to a § 1.111(b)-compliant reply will not be entered as a matter of right except when it is clearly limited to specified categories or filed during a suspended period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may enter a supplemental reply if clearly limited to: cancellation of claim(s); adoption of examiner suggestions; placement of the application in condition for allowance; reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply; correction of informalities; or simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed during a suspension under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c) must be entered. Examiner should annotate 'OK TO ENTER' if entered; 'DO NOT ENTER' and notify applicant if not entered. Supplemental replies reduce any accumulated patent term adjustment under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.147 for supplemental replies not approved for entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.147 to notify applicant that a supplemental reply was not entered because supplemental replies are not entered as a matter of right except as provided in 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include receipt date (37 CFR 1.6), and insert reason for non-entry (e.g., 'The supplemental reply is clearly not limited to placement of the application in condition for allowance'). Do not use if supplemental reply was entered or if it was filed during suspended period (such must be entered unless non-compliant under 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims presented without attempt to point out patentable novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims presented in an amendment make no attempt to point out patentable novelty, the claims should not be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment failing to point out the patentable novelty believed to be present may be held not fully responsive and a time period set to furnish a proper reply (MPEP § 714.03). If claims are clearly open to rejection on the record, a final rejection should generally be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate review of applicant actions near end of reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions filed near the end of the reply period should be reviewed as soon as possible upon availability to determine complete responsiveness and prevent abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check (A) proper signature, (B) filing within statutory or shortened time period, (C) full responsiveness and compliance with 37 CFR 1.121, (D) whether changes warrant transfer, (E) whether application is special, (F) if claims suggested for interference have been copied, (G) traversal of a restriction requirement, (H) whether applicant cited references, (I) whether a terminal disclaimer has been filed, and (J) whether security-related matter was added. If inadequate and sufficient time remains, notify applicant to complete the reply within the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action crosses amendment (supplemental action when amendment crosses in mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the Technology Center later, prepare a supplemental action promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental action need not reiterate all applicable portions of the previous action but should specify which portions are to be disregarded and indicate that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action. Heading: 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for permanent dark ink or equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires permanent dark ink or equivalent for papers that will become part of the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So-called 'easily erasable' paper may not provide a permanent copy. However, because papers are maintained in an Image File Wrapper, the type of paper is unlikely to be an issue so long as the Office can scan and reproduce the papers filed. See MPEP § 608.01 for more discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees when adding claims beyond previously paid-for counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must pay excess claims fees for each claim in excess of the previously paid number of independent and total claims before the examiner considers the new claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees: required for claims in excess of 3 independent claims or in excess of 20 total claims (dependent or independent). Multiple dependent claim fees are calculated based on the number of claims referred to. Nonelected claims withdrawn after restriction are included in determining fees for subsequent amendments unless canceled. Example provided illustrating how cancellations and additions affect the need for additional excess claim fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and other replies after final action (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final rejection or other final action are limited to certain types and may be admitted only under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted after final: (1) amendment canceling claims or complying with prior form requirement; (2) amendment presenting rejected claims in better form for appeal; (3) amendment touching the merits may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented. Admission or refusal does not relieve proceeding from appeal or abandonment conditions. Inter partes reexamination has additional restrictions (no amendment other than canceling claims after right of appeal except as provided).
